records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Feed HTML is imported with `raw_html` and later rendered via `raw post.cooked` without sanitization, allowing stored XSS from feed content.
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: TopicEmbed.import uses cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], post.rb's cook returns `raw` unprocessed for that method, RSS content from poll_feed (`TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`) flows in unsanitized, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Feed-controlled HTML (e.g., script tags via i.content) reaches the page unfiltered — stored XSS.

records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114 — Removing the `--category`/`-c` option is a breaking CLI regression that causes imported discussions to lose their selected category.
records.rationale: The diff verifiably removes `method_option :category` from disqus.thor and replaces the PostCreator call (which passed `category: category_id`) with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which has no category parameter — so imported topics can no longer be assigned a category. This is a real, specific, grounded behavior regression in the CLI's functionality that a maintainer should weigh (deliberate refactor vs. lost capability), though the new code path itself works as written, so it's a substantive scope/behavior concern rather than a code defect.
